body:
A VERDICT HANDSHAKE WENT MISSING AND THE COMMAND REPORTED WRITING IT. This is
the artefact the orchestrator reads to proceed, so it is worth a spec.

WHAT HAPPENED, measured:

  13:28  `aida review record BUG-1462 ... --pr 2059` printed:
             record:    .aida/review-verdicts/BUG-1462.json
             handshake: .aida/review-verdicts/PR-2059.json
                        (phase-3 handshake — the orchestrator reads this to proceed)

  13:40  BUG-1462.json   EXISTS, mtime 13:28     <- spec-keyed write succeeded
         PR-2059.json    ABSENT                   <- handshake write did not

  13:41  re-recorded at the SAME sha -> PR-2059.json now exists, 1876 bytes

SO IT IS INTERMITTENT, NOT DETERMINISTIC, AND THE COMMAND REPORTS SUCCESS
EITHER WAY. One of the two writes landed and the other did not, from a single
invocation, and stdout claimed both.

RULED OUT before reporting:
  - Not a clobber: the head never moved (62dfb3ebd80e both times) and I made
    no second record in between.
  - Not a cleanup: PR-2059 is OPEN, so a merged-PR sweep would not touch it.
  - Not a gap in the numbering: PR-2058.json and PR-2060.json both exist.
    2059 is the only hole in that range, out of 520 PR-keyed records.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING FILE: the PR-keyed handshake is what the
orchestrator reads. An approval whose handshake is silently absent presents to
the orchestrator as an UNREVIEWED PR — it stalls or re-reviews — while the
reviewer has a success message saying otherwise. The two seats disagree and
neither has a signal that they do.

AND THE ONLY REASON I FOUND IT IS THE SWEEP. It surfaced as `no-verdict:
[2059]` in the same scan I run for moved heads. Without that, the first
evidence would have been the orchestrator behaving as though #2059 were
unreviewed, which reads as an orchestrator fault rather than a write fault.

MY PRACTICE CHANGE, effective now: after every `review record`, stat the
handshake path the command printed. One `ls`, and it converts a claimed write
into an observed one. I have been requiring exactly this of other seats all
day — verify the artefact, not the claim about it — and applying it to
everything except my own tool's success message.

I am not filing it, per the standing directive. Disposition is yours. If it
helps: the distinguishing question for whoever takes it is whether the two
writes share a failure path or are independent, because a single invocation
landing one and not the other suggests they are not atomic — and an approval
that half-lands is worse than one that fails, since the spec record makes it
look recorded.

SEPARATELY: #2019 has moved past its refusal (b4ade573ef -> 442a63243c). That
is my next review.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: A verdict HANDSHAKE went missing while the command reported writing it - PR-2059, intermittent, spec record landed and handshake did not. The orchestrator reads that file
